newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- down, but outperforming.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- down, but outperforming.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were down at least 1/4 point at midday, but the continuing positive technical picture is lending support, traders said.
"The lack of supply is holding up the market pretty well," one trader said, explaining how munis have managed to avoid the steeper drops at midday in the U.S. Treasury market.
The government long bond was off 16/32 at 94-31/32 to yield 7.03 percent.
Treasuries lost ground after economic data was released earlier in the day.
The Conference Board said consumer confidence hit a 28-year high in May, jumping to 127.1. The number pushed an already sagging market lower as dealers worried about the implications for inflation.
"The market is worried about the strength of the economy and whether that's going to mean inflation," one muni trader said.
April durable goods, set for release on Wednesday, were seen by dealers as the next important data release this week. The figure was expected to show a 1.3 percent rise.
Tuesday's largest new issue is expected to be a $63 million New Mexico competitive refunding deal at 1300 EDT.
The week's supply picture was light, with about $2.1 bilion and 77 sales on the calendar, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
A highlight of the week was expected to be a nearly $234 million sale of general obligation bonds by the District of Columbia, which was slated for competitive sale on Wednesday.

In the secondary market, Broward County, Fla., Professional Sports Facilitites Tax Revnues Civic Arena Projects of 2028, which carry a 5-5/8 percent coupon and insurance from MBIA Insurance Corp., were bid at 5.74 percent, unchanged from Friday.
New York State Energy Research and Development Authority Gas Facilities Revenues of 2021, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon and MBIA insurance, were bid at 5.76 percent, up one basis point.
